subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Demonstrate presentation skills in a formal setting
Listen and respond to questions and feedback
Structure and grading of the Spoken Language Endorsement

questions.q: Which component of the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language A (4EA1) is the Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: Component 1
Component 2
Component 3
Component 4
questions.explain: In the 4EA1 specification the Spoken Language Endorsement is Component 3.

questions.q: How is the Spoken Language Endorsement reported on a candidate's result?
options: As a percentage added to the written paper marks
As a separate grade that does not contribute to the overall English Language grade
As part of the Component 1 reading mark
As a simple pass/fail only, merged into the final grade
questions.explain: The endorsement is reported separately and does not count towards the overall qualification grade.

questions.q: Which set of grades can be awarded for the Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: A*, A, B, C
Pass, Merit, Distinction
1 to 9
Fail, Pass, Credit, Honours
questions.explain: Candidates are awarded Pass, Merit or Distinction (or Not Classified).

questions.q: Apart from Pass, Merit and Distinction, what other outcome is possible for the endorsement?
options: Not Classified
Ungraded Credit
Provisional Pass
Deferred
questions.explain: A candidate who does not meet the Pass criteria is recorded as Not Classified.

questions.q: Who assesses a candidate's performance for the Spoken Language Endorsement?
options: An external examiner who visits the centre
The candidate's own teacher within the centre
A panel of other candidates
Pearson staff by video recording only
questions.explain: The endorsement is internally assessed by the candidate's teacher.

questions.q: What form does the assessed task for the endorsement take?
options: A written essay read aloud only
A formal presentation followed by responding to questions
A group debate with no individual assessment
A recorded telephone conversation
questions.explain: Candidates give a formal presentation and then respond to questions and feedback.

questions.q: Which variety of English are candidates required to use in the presentation?
options: Regional dialect vocabulary
Spoken Standard English
Informal text-message language
Any language of the candidate's choice
questions.explain: One assessment objective requires candidates to use spoken Standard English effectively.

questions.q: After delivering the presentation, what must the candidate do?
options: Write a reflective evaluation immediately
Respond to questions and feedback from the audience
Repeat the presentation a second time
Mark another candidate's presentation
questions.explain: Listening and responding to questions and feedback is a required part of the task.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the setting in which the presentation should be delivered?
options: A casual, unplanned chat with a friend
A formal setting, such as to the teacher and class
A private one-to-one interview with no audience
An online forum post
questions.explain: The presentation is delivered in a formal setting, typically to the teacher and class.

questions.q: Which aspect of a candidate's speech does 'Standard English' primarily concern?
options: Their regional accent
Their grammar and vocabulary
The volume of their voice
Their choice of visual aids
questions.explain: Standard English refers to grammar and vocabulary, not to a particular accent.

questions.q: Why is the endorsement grade reported separately rather than folded into the overall grade?
options: Because spoken language is graded 1 to 9 like the written papers
Because it is an endorsement of spoken skills reported alongside, not within, the qualification grade
Because it replaces one of the written components
Because it is worth exactly 20% of the qualification
questions.explain: As an endorsement, it recognises spoken skills separately and does not alter the overall grade.

questions.q: Which behaviour best demonstrates effective presentation skills in a formal setting?
options: Reading every word from a script in a flat monotone with no eye contact
Speaking clearly and confidently, using structure and engaging the audience
Talking as quickly as possible to finish early
Improvising with no preparation or structure
questions.explain: Clear, structured, confident delivery that engages the audience shows strong presentation skills.

questions.q: A candidate speaks with a strong regional accent but uses correct standard grammar and vocabulary. How should this be judged for the Standard English objective?
options: It fails, because Standard English requires a neutral accent
It can still meet the objective, because Standard English concerns grammar and vocabulary, not accent
It automatically earns a Distinction regardless of content
It cannot be assessed at all
questions.explain: Standard English can be spoken in any accent; only grammar and vocabulary are relevant.

questions.q: Responding appropriately to audience questions mainly demonstrates a candidate's ability to do what?
options: Memorise a script word for word
Listen carefully and develop or clarify their ideas in reply
Avoid difficult questions by changing the subject
Read visual aids aloud
questions.explain: Effective responses show active listening and the ability to extend or clarify ideas.

questions.q: Why is the candidate usually free to choose (or be given) a topic they can speak about in depth?
options: So the presentation can be marked by other candidates
So they can sustain a substantial, well-developed formal presentation
So the presentation lasts as long as possible
So they can avoid using Standard English
questions.explain: A suitable topic lets the candidate develop and sustain their ideas across the presentation.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Pearson's monitoring of centres' Spoken Language Endorsement assessments?
options: To re-mark every candidate's written papers
To help ensure the assessment standards are applied consistently across centres
To choose the topic for each candidate
To convert the endorsement into a numerical grade
questions.explain: Monitoring supports consistent application of the endorsement standards between centres.

questions.q: Which response to an unexpected, challenging audience question best shows the required listening-and-response skill?
options: Ignoring the question and repeating an earlier point
Acknowledging the question and giving a relevant, developed answer
Saying only 'I don't know' and stopping
Asking the audience member to withdraw the question
questions.explain: A relevant, developed reply shows the candidate has listened and can respond thoughtfully.

questions.q: Which sentence would a candidate be expected to use to meet the spoken Standard English objective?
options: We was well happy about them results, innit
We were very pleased with the results
Me and him done the project dead good
They ain't got no reason to complain
questions.explain: This sentence uses standard grammar and vocabulary appropriate to a formal presentation.

questions.q: During his assessment, Omar reads his entire presentation word-for-word from cards, mumbling, with no eye contact and little expression. Which objective is he most clearly failing to meet?
options: Demonstrating presentation skills in a formal setting
Using written punctuation accurately
Producing a bibliography of sources
Marking his own performance
questions.explain: Mumbling, no eye contact and flat delivery show weak presentation skills.

questions.q: After Priya's presentation, a classmate asks her to justify a claim she made. Priya restates her point clearly, adds a new example and links back to her argument. Which objective does this best evidence?
options: Using visual aids
Listening and responding to questions and feedback
Writing under timed conditions
Reading an unseen text
questions.explain: Extending her answer with an example shows she listened and responded effectively.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language (Spec A) (4EA1) specification; Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement
